paragraphs.text: To the same purpose with the former, {Jer 32:1} which is reckoned his fourteenth sermon, as this his fifteenth; by both we see that "the word of God is not bound," though the preacher may; {2Ti 2:9} "It runs and is glorified," is free and not fettered. {2Th 3:1}
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover, the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah the second time.

paragraphs.text: God forsaketh not his prisoners, but giveth them oft extraordinary comforts. Philip, Landgrave of Hesse, being a long time held prisoner by Charles V for the defence of the gospel, was demanded what upheld him all that time? he answered, Divinas martyrum consolationes se sensisse, that he felt in his soul the divine consolations of martyrs, in whom as the afflictions of Christ do abound, so do comforts by Christ abound much more. {2Co 1:5}
paragraphs.anchor: While he was yet shut up.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Of the promise of restoration. {Jer 32:41-44} Or of Jerusalem, which he is said to make in the sense that he "made Moses and Aaron," that is, "advanced" them. {1Sa 12:6, marg.}
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord the maker thereof.

paragraphs.text: Jehovah the essentiator, who giveth being to all things, and particularly to his word.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord is his name.

paragraphs.text: Thou hast a promise, and I will perform it; but so as that thou Jeremiah, and such as thou art, Daniel, Ezekiel, Nehemiah, &c., pray over the promise. The angel told Daniel he came for his prayer’s sake. {Jer 10:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Call unto me, and I will answer thee.

paragraphs.text: Or, Abstruse and reserved things. God’s praying people get to know much of his mind above others; like as John, by weeping, got the book opened; and Daniel, by prayer, had the king’s secret revealed unto him in a night vision. {Dan 2:18-19} Bene orasse, est bene studuisse, said Luther; who, because he had much communion with God by prayer, so holy truths were daily more and more made known unto him, he knew not how nor which way, as himself said.
paragraphs.anchor: And show thee great and mighty things.

paragraphs.text: Or, Catapults, or engines of demolition, used to batter with. See Jer 32:24.
paragraphs.anchor: Which are thrown down by the mounts.

paragraphs.text: Or, Mattocks - scil., After that the enemy had entered the city, and cried, as Psa 137:3,
paragraphs.anchor: And by the sword.

paragraphs.text: “ Destruite, ex imis subvertite fundamentis: ”
Down with it, down with it, even to the ground.

But they fight not in God’s name; for he hath, for all their wickedness, hidden his face from them; therefore they fight with such sorry success; the houses which they would defend are filled with their dead caresses. This whole verse would be hemmed in with a parenthesis.
paragraphs.anchor: They come to fight with the Chaldeans.

paragraphs.text: Una eademque manus vulnus opemque feret. This is God’s usual method and manner of dealing with his people, {Hos 6:1} as a skilful physician, primo pungit, deinde ungit.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I will bring it health and cure.

paragraphs.text: “ Enecat, ut possit vivificare Deus. ”

And I will reveal {a} unto them abundance of peace and truth.] Why then, feri, Domine, feri; such gold as "peace and truth" cannot be bought too dear. The Chaldee here hath it, Revelabo iis portam poenitentiae, I will reveal unto them the gate of repentance, and show them how they may walk in the way of peace and truth.
{a} Revelabo., i.e., re ipsa exhibebo.
As Jer 24:5; Jer 30:3; Jer 32:44. They shall be as if I had not cast them off, and I will hear them. {Zec 10:6}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will cause the captivity of Judah.

paragraphs.text: Which must therefore needs be a filthy and loathsome thing, else what need cleansing? Christ, for this cause, came by water and blood.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity.

paragraphs.text: This clause expoundeth the former, and containeth the mother mercy.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will pardon all their iniquities.

paragraphs.text: And it shall be to me a name {a} of joy,] i.e., An honour, that I shall take singular delight in.
Which bodes no good to them; for the Church’s welfare is ever joined with the downfall and destruction of her enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness.

paragraphs.text: {a} In nomen laetum, i.e., laeificum.
God loveth to help his people, when they are forsaken of their hopes.
paragraphs.anchor: Again there shall be heard in this place.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 7:34; Jer 16:9.
paragraphs.anchor: The voice of joy.

paragraphs.text: This carmen intercalare the Jews sang joyfully at their return from Babylon, {Ezr 3:11} and the saints shall have cause to sing throughout all eternity.
paragraphs.anchor: The voice of them that shall say, Praise the Lord of hosts, for he is good.

paragraphs.text: Even "the calves of their lips, giving thanks to his name," {Heb 13:15} together with other evangelical sacrifices, as contrition; {Psa 51:17} confidence; {Psa 4:4} alms deeds; {Heb 13:16} the obedience of faith; {Rom 15:16} self-denial, {Rom 12:1} &c. The Talmudists say that the sacrifice of praise here mentioned shall continue when all other sacrifices are abolished; and this we see verified in the Christian Church.
paragraphs.anchor: And of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Several sorts of buildings, yea, even sheep cotes and lodges for shepherds and their flocks. All these promises are antitheta, opposite to those menaces, Jer 7:34; Jer 16:9; cf. Jer 25:10; Jer 31:24.
paragraphs.anchor: In all the cities thereof shall be an habitation of shepherds

paragraphs.text: As shepherds used oft to tell their sheep. Christ the great Shepherd and Bishop of souls knoweth all his sheep, and calleth them by name; he hath them ever in numerato, for he numbereth the stars also. See Joh 10:3; Joh 10:11-12.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall the flocks pass again under the hand of him that telleth them.

paragraphs.text: Praestabo verbum istud optimum, as Tremellius well rendereth it. I will perform that best word or promise, viz., concerning Christ, in whom all the former and future promises are Yea and Amen, to the glory of God. {2Co 1:20}
paragraphs.anchor: I will perform that good thing.

paragraphs.text: “ Haec dicenda bono sunt bona verba die. ”

See the same, Jer 23:5. The sweet promise concerning Christ can never be too often repeated. The Greek and German versions have that clause here also as there, "And a king shall reign and prosper, or understand."
paragraphs.anchor: I will cause the branch of righteousness.

paragraphs.text: Heb., This is that he shall call her, Jehovah our righteousness; called the Church shall be by Christ’s own name, which is a very high honour, as being his spouse, and making up one mystical body with him. Hence she is called "Christ," {1Co 12:12} and "the fulness of him who filleth all in all." {Eph 1:23} See Jer 23:6, with Eze 48:35.
paragraphs.anchor: And this is the name wherewith she shall be called, The Lord is our righteousness.

paragraphs.text: The man Christ Jesus. {Luk 1:32-33}
paragraphs.anchor: David shall never want a man.

paragraphs.text: The same man Christ Jesus, who is, as a King everlasting, so a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek; and his sacrificing of himself once is more than equivalent to the daily perpetual sacrificing. Whereunto may be added the continuance of an evangelical ministry in the Church to the world’s end. {Mat 28:20 Eph 4:11-13}
paragraphs.anchor: Neither shall the priest want a man.

paragraphs.text: Iterum de perpetuitate regni Christi tractat et iurat, saith Oecolampadius. Once more he treateth of the perpetuity of Christ’s kingdom, and assureth it as by oath.
paragraphs.anchor: And the word of the Lord, &c.

paragraphs.text: God hath hitherto kept promise with nights and days, that one shall succeed the other; and will he not then keep in touch with his people?
paragraphs.anchor: If ye can break my covenant of the day.

paragraphs.text: See Jer 33:17-18. The poet hath somewhat like this:
paragraphs.anchor: Then may also my covenant.

paragraphs.text: “ Iungantur ante saeva sideribus freta,
Et ignis undae, tartaro tristi polus,
Lux alma tenebris, roscidae nocti dies, ”& c.
- Sen. in Octavia.
See Gen 13:16; Gen 15:5.
paragraphs.anchor: As the host of heaven.

paragraphs.text: True believers.
paragraphs.anchor: So will I multiply the seed of David.

paragraphs.text: Godly ministers. See Psa 68:11.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Levites.

paragraphs.text: Or, Again. Idem repetit; the same thing is repeated, that it may be the better believed.
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover.

paragraphs.text: This unbelieving, misgiving, desponding people of mine.
paragraphs.anchor: Consider thou not what this people have spoken.

paragraphs.text: Iudah et Israel habentur pro properipsemate.
paragraphs.anchor: The two families.

paragraphs.text: See on Jer 33:20. If there be not a constant intercourse of either.
paragraphs.anchor: If my covenant be not with day and night.

paragraphs.text: The body of the faithful, whom he ruleth by his Word and Spirit. {Psa 105:1; Psa 105:6 Rom 9:6 Gal 3:16-17; Gal 6:16}
paragraphs.anchor: Then will I cast away the seed of Jacob.

paragraphs.text: This is a complexive promise, and better than money, answereth all things.
paragraphs.anchor: And will have mercy on them.
